chains.title: Alt-specific GABPA binding activates TERT

links.claim: The alt allele creates or strengthens an ETS-family binding site, with GABPA binding more strongly than ref. GABPA is chosen from the ETS family because TERT promoter mutations are canonical de novo ETS motifs and GABPA/GABPB is a plausible activator in glioblastoma. QBiC-SELEX coverage: not_checked, since no evidence list or screen row was provided.
The alt allele lies within the TERT promoter and alters a local cis-regulatory element.
Increased GABPA binding at the mutant TERT promoter increases TERT transcription.
In glioblastoma cells, this GABPA-dependent TERT promoter activation increases telomerase activity.
Increased telomerase activity supports telomere maintenance and tumor cell immortalization in glioblastoma.

predictions: Alt allele shows stronger GABPA binding than ref.
GABPA occupies the mutant TERT promoter in glioblastoma cells.
GABPA loss reduces alt-linked TERT expression and telomerase activity.
falsified_if: Allele-specific binding assays show no alt-dependent GABPA enrichment in glioblastoma cells.
GABPA is not expressed or not nuclear in the relevant glioblastoma context.
Alt-specific TERT expression is unaffected by GABPA knockdown or inhibition.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: No TF-mediated allelic effect at this variant.
Any disease association is due to a linked causal variant, a passenger mutation at a mutational hotspot, or no allelic effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific reporter or binding assays show a reproducible alt-dependent TF effect at this exact variant.
The variant is shown to be the causal allele rather than a linked passenger or hotspot mutation.

chains.title: Alt-specific ETS1 binding activates TERT

links.claim: The alt allele creates or strengthens an ETS-family binding site that binds ETS1 more strongly than ref. ETS1 is an alternative ETS-family member that could recognize the same mutant motif. QBiC-SELEX coverage: not_checked; no evidence list or screen row was provided.
The variant is in the TERT promoter and changes a cis-regulatory element.
Alt-specific ETS1 binding increases TERT transcription.
In glioblastoma cells, ETS1-dependent activation of TERT increases telomerase activity.
Higher telomerase activity promotes telomere maintenance and tumor growth.

predictions: Alt allele shows stronger ETS1 binding than ref.
ETS1 occupies the mutant TERT promoter in glioblastoma cells.
ETS1 loss reduces alt-linked TERT expression.
falsified_if: No alt-specific ETS1 binding is detected at the TERT promoter.
ETS1 knockdown does not change alt-linked TERT expression.
ETS1 is not expressed in the relevant glioblastoma cells.

chains.title: Alt-specific ELK1 binding modulates TERT

links.claim: The alt allele creates or strengthens an ETS-family site that binds ELK1 more strongly than ref. ELK1 is another ETS-family candidate for the mutant motif, but this chain is less likely without direct evidence. QBiC-SELEX coverage: not_checked; no evidence list or screen row was provided.
The variant is in the TERT promoter and alters a cis-regulatory element.
Alt-specific ELK1 binding modulates TERT transcription; the direction may depend on context, so this chain does not assume binding equals activation without evidence.
In glioblastoma cells, ELK1-dependent regulation of TERT changes telomerase activity.
Altered telomerase activity contributes to telomere maintenance and tumor phenotype.

predictions: Alt allele shows stronger ELK1 binding than ref.
ELK1 occupies the mutant TERT promoter.
ELK1 perturbation changes TERT expression in the relevant cells.
falsified_if: ELK1 does not bind the alt allele preferentially.
ELK1 loss does not alter TERT expression in glioblastoma cells.
The effect is fully explained by another ETS factor.

matrix.test: Allele-specific EMSA or biotinylated-oligo pull-down with glioblastoma nuclear extract, comparing ref and alt TERT promoter oligos, followed by anti-GABPA supershift; if needed, run anti-ETS1 in parallel to separate H1 from H2/H3.

outcomes.outcome: Alt-specific shift not supershifted by anti-GABPA
Alt-specific shift not supershifted by anti-GABPA

next_experiment: Allele-specific EMSA or DNA pull-down using ref versus alt TERT promoter oligos and glioblastoma nuclear extract, with anti-GABPA supershift. This directly separates the top two chains, H1 (alt-specific GABPA binding) and H0 (no TF-mediated allelic effect), at low cost; adding anti-ETS1 in the same experiment would also help distinguish H2 from H1.
